cards.text: Jesus is walking out of the temple with His disciples. One of them stops and stares up: “Teacher, look at the magnificent stones and buildings!” Friend, that's the face you make driving past a house you will NEVER be able to afford.

cards.question: Jesus looks at those same great buildings. What does He say will happen to them?

answers.text: Every stone will be thrown down
They will be covered in gold
They will stand for all time

cards.text: Later Jesus sits on the Mount of Olives, right across from the temple. Four of His disciples come to Him privately: Peter, James, John and Andrew.

cards.question: Peter, James, John and Andrew ask Jesus when these things will happen. What else do they want to know?

answers.text: The sign that it's about to happen
Where they should go to hide
Whether they may tell the others

cards.question: Jesus starts answering the four of them with a warning. What must they not let anyone do to them?

cards.text: Jesus says many will come in His name, claiming, ‘I am He,’ and will deceive many. It's the text saying you won a cruise you never entered: sounds official, is NOT.

cards.question: When the disciples hear of wars and rumors of wars, Jesus tells them not to be ___.
Jesus says that when those wars come, the end has arrived.

cards.text: Jesus keeps the list coming: nation against nation, kingdom against kingdom, earthquakes in various places, and famines. Friend, my mustache is gripping the counter just HEARING it.

cards.question: Wars, earthquakes, famines. Jesus gives a picture for all of it. What does He call them?

answers.text: The first drops of a storm
The first cracks in a wall

cards.text: Then Jesus tells the four to be on their guard. They'll be delivered over to the councils and beaten in the synagogues.

cards.question: Jesus says that on His account the disciples will stand before governors and kings as judges over them.
Jesus says something has to happen first: the ___ must be proclaimed to all the nations.

cards.text: Jesus says when they're arrested and handed over, don't worry beforehand about what to say. No rehearsing your big speech in the shower ELEVEN times the night before!

cards.question: When the disciples are arrested, Jesus says it won't be them speaking. It will be the Holy ___.

cards.text: Then it gets hard. Brother will betray brother to death, a father his child, and children will rise against their parents.

cards.question: Jesus warns the four that they'll be hated by everyone because of His name.
Hated by everyone. But Jesus gives a promise. Who will be saved?

answers.text: The one who perseveres to the end
The one who is never arrested
The one who knows the day

cards.text: Jesus gets specific. He talks about seeing “the abomination of desolation standing where it should not be (let the reader understand),” and when that happens, people need to move.

cards.question: When they see the abomination of desolation, what does Jesus tell those in Judea to do?

cards.text: And Jesus means GO: anyone on the housetop shouldn't go back inside to retrieve anything from his house. It's the fire alarm at work, friend, and you do NOT go back to your desk for your mug.

cards.question: Someone out working in the field shouldn't go back for his ___.

cards.text: In all that rush, Jesus names the ones who'd have it hardest, friend: “How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers!”

cards.question: Running for the mountains is hard enough. Jesus tells them to pray it won't happen in the ___.

cards.text: Jesus calls them “days of tribulation unseen from the beginning of God’s creation until now, and never to be seen again.” Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer, and I'm not even putting that in the same sentence.

cards.question: Days that hard. What has the Lord done with those days, for the sake of the elect whom He has chosen?
Jesus says that if the Lord had not cut those days short, nobody would be saved.

cards.text: Then Jesus comes back to the warning He started with. At that time, someone might say, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘There He is!’

cards.question: If someone says, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ Jesus tells the disciples to go and see for themselves.

cards.text: False Christs and false prophets will appear and perform signs and wonders. Like that "bank" email with the logo and everything: looks real, is NOT your bank.

cards.question: Those false Christs and false prophets will try to deceive even whom, if that were possible?
Jesus tells the four to be on their guard. What has He already done for them?

answers.text: Sent an angel to guard them

cards.text: And that's where we'll pause, friend. Jesus is still sitting on that mountain, and He is NOT done teaching, so keep that apron on.

findings.problem: The joke opens with "It's the text saying you won a cruise." In a Bible lesson, "the text" can easily be read as the Bible text, not a phone text message. A baker has to stop and work out what the comparison means.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: The right answer "Spirit" stands out. It is the only capitalized word and the only singular one, so it is the only answer that fits "It will be the Holy ___." The plural, lowercase "angels" and "prophets" read awkwardly in the blank.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: "Jesus names the ones who'd have it hardest" adds a superlative the text doesn't give. Mark 13:17 says only, "How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers!" It never says they have it hardest of anyone.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: This joke is the same comparison as stop 1, card 6: a scam message that looks official but is fake ("sounds official, is NOT" and then "looks real, is NOT your bank"). The same image and punchline shape come back in one walkthrough. The docs say there's no formula, but they don't say whether a comparison can be reused within a lesson.
findings.question: Should Papa Dorin avoid reusing the same comparison or punchline shape within one walkthrough, even when the passage repeats its theme (here, deception in Mark 13:6 and 13:22)?

findings.problem: The last story card is only the "story isn't over" line, but it cites Mark 13:23. It tells nothing from 13:23. Its only Bible detail, Jesus sitting on the mountain, comes from Mark 13:3. The docs allow this card to be just the line when the last verse was asked on a choice card, but they don't say what it should cite.
findings.question: What should a closing card cite when it is only the "story isn't over" line: the passage's last verse, the verse its detail comes from (here Mark 13:3), or no verses at all?
